Habibul lslam Bhuiyan, Senior Advocate, M Qumrul Haque Siddique, Tushar Kanti Roy, Sattya Ranjan Mondal, Advocates-----For the Appellant. 
Mahmudul Islam, Senior Advocate with Shah MdMunir Sharif Abdul Momen Chowdhury, AKM NurulAlam, Sohel Raila & lmran Jahangir; Advocates-----For the Respondents 1-3.

Mohammad Ali ----- Respondents
full_judgment:
Nozrul Islam ChowdhuryJ : This appeal has a chequered story to tell. The property involved in the suit being Other Class Suit No, 3 of 2010 was mortgaged by Capital Ship Breakers Ltd. to Islami Bank (Bangladesh) Limited as co-lateral security of loan availed by M/s MA Salam and Company; thereafter on 4-11-91 Capital Ship Breakers deposited title deeds relating to the said suit property with lslami Bank Bangladesh Limited with a view to secure the credit facilities advanced by the respondent Bank but eventually the loan was not repaid by the borrower as a result Islami Bank Bangladesh Limited (herein after referred to as respondent bank) instituted Artha Rin Adalat Suit No. 29 of 2005 for realization of loan amount of Tk. 51,73,81735,02 before the Artha Rin Adalat, 1st Court, Chittagong impleading Capital Ship Breakers as defendant No,

2. The suit was contested by Capital Ship Breakers Ltd and eventually it was decreed ex-parte on 26-6-05 with a direction upon the judgment debtor to pay the decreetal dues to the respondent Bank within 60(sixty) days but the judgment debtor did not pay the decreetal amount so the respondent Bank filed Artha Rin Execution Case No. 340 of 2005 before the same Court, During pendency of the execution case both the judgment debtor and the decree holder Bank (Islami Bank Bangladesh Ltd) compromised the matter amicably upon filing a solenarna. The Artha Rin Adalat, 1st Court, Chittagong accepted the said solenama and the execution case were disposed of according to the terms of the said solenama. As per the terms and condition of the said solenama the judgment debtor was to pay Taka 8(eight) crore as was stipulated in the solenama and in case of failure of selling the mortgaged property within 12 months the decree holder bank would have absolute right to sell the mortgaged property through Court and accordingly on failure to repay the decreetal amount the bank filed an application for restoration of the said execution case because of non-compliance of the terms of the compromise as referred to above, whereupon the execution case was restored to its original file and number. Thereafter, the judgment debtor Messrs Salam and Company brought Writ Petition No. 4070 of 2008 before the High Court Division relating to the proceedings of the said Execution Case No. 340 of 2005 which was rejected summarily on 4-6-2008 by a Division Bench of this Court, thereafter the petitioner Salam and Company being aggrieved by the said judgment and order dated 4-6-2008 passed by the High Court Division in Writ Petition No. 4070 of 2008 preferred Civil Petition For Leave To Appeal No. 1287 of 2008 before the Appellate Division but the said Leave Petition was dismissed on 12-5-2009 thereafter the petitioner preferred Civil Review Petition No. 49 of 2009 before the Appellate Division but the same was also dismissed for default.

3. After disposal of Civil Review Petition No. 49 of 2009 the petitioner in Writ Petition No. 4070 of 2008 filed another Writ Petition being No. 6115 of 2008 challenging the order No. 42 dated 30-7-2008 passed by the Artha Rin Adalat, 1st Court, Chittagong in Artha Rin Execution Case No. 340 of 2005 and in the said Writ Petition two sister concerns of M A Salam and Company namely Messrs Elly Enterprise and Messrs Munna Trading Agency were petitioner Nos. 1 and 2 whereupon Rule was issued in the said Writ Petition No. 6115 of2008 but the same was also discharged by a Division Bench of this Court on 25-6-2006.

4. Thereafter in the said Execution Case No. 340 of 2005 the property was sold to Mr Mohammad Ali son of Badiur Rahman of Chittagong Commercial Area i.e. respondent No. 1 herein ( the suit property along with other land) vide order No. 37 dated 17-4-2008 at a price of Taka 4,05,000,00 and the said sale was confirmed vide order dated 23- 6-2099, therefore, according to the case of the respondent , upon confirmation of the sale on 23-6- 2009 the title of the purchased property vested upon the auction purchaser (respondent No. 1). Accordingly the respondent Bank handed over all the title deeds relating to the property involved, to the auction purchaser Mr Mohammad Ali vide a letter under reference No. IBBL/ Agra/2009/1779 dated 30-11-2009 thereafter; the sale certificate was registered on 25-11-2009 in favour of the auction purchaser (respondent No. 1).

5. Meanwhile, MA Salam one of the director of Capital Ship Breakers Limited brought Writ Petition No. 4180 of 2009 challenging the order dated 26-2-2008 passed by the Altha Rin Adalat, 1st Court, Chittagong in Execution Case No. 340 of 2005 restoring the execution case to its file and number, whereupon this Court issued a rule with an order of stay but subsequently upon an application filed by the decree holder (respondent bank) this Court vacated the order of stay on 16-11-2009 and it was a150 directed by this Court that the Artha Rin Adalat, 1st Court, Chittagong to proceed with the Artha Rin Adalat Case No. 340 of 2005 in accordance with law. Thereafter, being aggrieved by the aforesaid order Mr MA Salam as a director of Capital Ship Breakers as a petitioner preferred Civil Petition For Leave To Appeal No. 2278 of 2009 but in the meantime the Rule issued in Writ Petition No. 4180 of 2009 came up for hearing and a Division Bench of this Court vide judgment and order dated 2-3-2010 discharged the Rule with costs of Taka 3 (three) lakhs.

6. Being aggrieved by the aforesaid judgment the Capital Ship Breakers preferred Civil Petition For Leave To Appeal No. 808 of 2008 but both the aforesaid two Civil Petition For Leave to Appeals were dismissed; one was dismissed as being not pressed and Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 808 of 2008 was dismissed on merit.

7. During pendency of the Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal the appellant Ayat Steels Limited as plaintiff instituted Other Suit No.3 of 2010 before the Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Chittagong seeking a declaration of title over the property involved in the suit which was the subject matter of Altha Rin Execution Case No. 340 of 2005 arising out of Artha Rin suit No. 29 of 2005, the said suit was instituted impleading the decree holder bank i.e. Islami Bank Bangladesh Limited and its Agrabad Branch as defendant Nos. 2 and 3 while the auction purchaser Mohammad Ali as defendant No.1. During pendency of the Other Suit No.3 of 2010 the plaintiff filed an application under Order XXXIX, rule 1 and 2 read with section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure praying for temporary injunction whereupon the defendant Nos. 1-3 entered appearance filing written objection, thereafter the injunction matter came up for hearing on 4-3-2010, meanwhile another application for temporary injunction was filed by the plaintiff before the trial Court but the said application was kept with the record by the learned Joint District Judge by his order dated 4-3-2010. The plaintiff as petitioner preferred Civil Revision No. 1020 of 2010 before this Court and obtained rule on 14-3-2010 with a direction upon the parties to maintain status quo for a period of 3 (three) months, but at the same time this Court also directed the learned Joint District Judge to dispose of the injunction petition within 30 days from the date of receipt of its order. Thereafter on 6-5-2010 after hearing both sides the learned Joint District Judge rejected the application for injunction.

8. Being aggrieved by the aforesaid order the plaintiff as appellant brought FMAT No. 288 of 2010 subsequently re-numbered as FMA No. 137 of 2010 and upon a separate application for injunction this Court issued Civil Rule No. 421 (fm) of 2010 on 21-7-2010 with an ad-interim order of injunction upon the opposite party Nos. 1-3 i.e. respondent Nos. 1-3. The said appeal and Civil Revision No. 421 (fm) 2010 are being disposed of by this Court by this single judgment.

9. Facts narrated by the appellant also includes that on 6-4-2008 Ayat Steels Limited i.e. the appellant was incorporated as a Private Limited Company and that subsequently on 1-6-2009 Ayat Steels Ltd -entered into a contract for purchase of 4.12 acres of land situated at Sitalpur from Capital Ship Breakers Ltd, thereafter on 10-8-2009 Ayat Steels Ltd obtained Non-Encumbrance Certificate from the Sub Registry office, thereafter on 30-11- 2009 the sale deed in respect of the said land was executed by Capital Ship Breakers Ltd in favour of the appellant Ayat Steels Ltd upon personal appearance of the three executants before the Sub-registrar's office for the purpose of registration of the said deed on 2-12-2009 followed by delivery of possession, thereafter on 30-12-2009 one of the remaining executants appeared before the Sub-registrar office and got his part registered. Meanwhile, on December 3 and 4, 2009 some officers of Islami Bank Bangladesh Ltd threatened the appellant of dispossession, consequently on December 6 Ayat Steels Limited lodged an application under section, 44 of the Criminal Procedure, thereafter on 30-12-2009 Mr Mohammad Ali also threatened to dispossess, consequently on 4-12-2010 Ayat Steels Limited instituted Other Class Suit No.3 of 2010 seeking a declaration of its title, confirmation of possessions and perpetual injunction over its purchased 4.12 acres of land as aforesaid impleading Mohammad Ali and Islami Bank Bangladesh Limited as also the said vendors of the appellant as defendants and upon institution of the suit a separate application for injunction under Order XXXIX Rule 1 and 2 of the Code of Civil Procedure was filed by the appellant praying for temporary injunction and upon receipt of notice the respondent No. I Mohammad Ali, respondent Nos. 2 and 3 entered appearance upon filing written objection and upon hearing both sides the learned Joint District Judge, refused the prayer for interim injunction by his order dated 4-3-2010 and the said order of refusal was challenged before this Court in Civil Revision No. 1020 of 2010 (albeit a misconceived one) and upon the said revisional application a direction was passed by this Court to maintain status quo in respect of possession of the suit land with a further direction to get the temporary injunction petition heard within 30 (thirty) days from the date of receipt of the order. Upon receipt of the said order passed by this Court on 14-3-2010 the learned Joint District Judge took up the application for temporary injunction once again for disposal and after hearing both sides he found it proper to refuse the prayer for temporary injunction by his order dated 6-5-2010. Challenging the aforesaid order dated 6-5-2010 the plaintiff Ayat Steels Ltd as appellant preferred this appeal.

10. Mr Habibul Islam Bhuiyan, the learned Counsel appearing with Mr Qumrul Haque Siddique, submits that the Court below failed to construe the expression prima facie case involved in a suit and prima facie case means and amounts to a question of law to be tried in the suit and in elaborating his submission Mr Bhuiyan drew our attention to section 58 of the Transfer of Property Act which defines mortgage, while clause (f) of section 58 defines mortgage by depositing title deeds and then submits, such a provision cannot be taken lightly and cannot be permitted to be exercised frequently so as to render section 59 of the same Act a redundant one particularly in view of the fact that clause (f) of section 58 is an exception to the main provision of section 58, therefore, the provision of clause (f) of section 58 by which mortgage by depositing the title deed is permitted, has to be constructed very strictly and the said provision of law namely clause (f) of section 58 of Transfer of Property Act presupposes an urban character and that the place of deposit of title deed should be a urban area and such a position according to Mr Bhuiyan has been fortified by very many decisions.

11. It is also argued by Mr Bhuiyan that plain reading of the provision of law also gives a clear idea that if it is an agreement to secure debt must be registered to create a valid mortgage. In cases where loan has been given earlier and subsequently the borrower deposits his deeds of immovable property with intent to create security it becomes a valid mortgage though there is no registered instrument. But this avenue is not open to those who want to take a loan on the basis of an agreement to secure the loan by mortgage but to avoid payment of revenue deposit title deed under a memorandum. In the present case title deeds were taken earlier and the money was lent on the basis of several subsequent agreements as per statements made in the plaint of Artha Rin Suit it does not show any relationship with the loans given and the title deeds deposited. The transaction as entered into shows that the deposit of title deeds and sanction of loan to M/s Capital Ship Breakers are different set of transaction. No legal relationship of security for the loan is visible or even assumable in the two sets of events. Referring to all these Mr Bhuiyan submits that as a matter of fact there was no valid mortgage ever took place between the Bank and the borrower Capital Ship Breakers.

12. To substantiate his submissions as above, Mr Bhuiyan placed reliance in the case of PT Krishnaswami Ayyangar vs Chevula Kamalamma AIR 1941 PC 90 (92); (Obla) Sundarachriar vs Narayan Ayyar AIR 1931 PC 36 (38 and 39); M Subramanian vs MLBM Lutchman AIR 1923 PC 50 (53); Eagle Star Insurance Co Ltd vs Usman Sons Ltd PLD 1969 Karachi 123 (125. 126. 135. 136 para13 and page 140 para18).

13. MrBhuiyan submits further that in the absence of valid mortgage Artha Rin Adalat acquired no legal authority to transfer the suit land without converting the decree into one against persons impleaded as defendants and that too without complying with the procedure for attachment and issuance of sale proclamation as provided by Rule 44 to 66 of Order XXI of the Code of Civil Procedure, therefore, Mr Bhuiyan submits that in the absence of such proceedings the alleged sale by the Artha Rin Adalat and the executing Court to Mr Mohammad Ali apparently confers no title and therefore, bainama (sale certificate of land under Order XXI, rule 94 of the Code of Civil Procedure) conveys no title over the suit land in favour of Mohammad Ali the respondent No. 1, thus the trial Court ought to have held that a prima facie title on the suit land is in favour of the plaintiff appellant and a contrary view is not sustainable.

14. It is also submitted by Mr Bhuiyan that the argument to the effect that the claim of title by Ayat Steels is barred by res judicata is not also sustain- able in law because of reasons more than one such as section II of the Code of Civil Procedure bar subsequent suits provided the Court trying earlier suit is competent to try the later one but in the present case that Artha Rin Adalat which tried Artha Rin Suit No. 29 of 2005 is a Court of limited jurisdiction and is not competent to try the issues raised in the subsequent suit namely the instant suit brought by Ayat Steels Ltd.

15. To substantiate his submission to the effect as above, Mr Bhuiyan placed reliance in the case of Al-Baraka Bank vs Rina Alam reported in 56 DLR 588.

16. Secondly, the plea of res judicata in the facts and circumstances of the case is not available at this stage inasmuch as question of maintainability of the suit cannot be gone into at the time of deciding an interlocutory matter like the prayer for temporary injunction and for this purpose Mr Bhuiyan placed reliance in the case of Dacca Match Factory vs Bangladesh Match Factory Co. 30 DLR 244, Nasir Mia vs Anwar Hossain 48 DLR 28. Molla Mahajeaul Islam vs Slate 53 DLR 552.

17. Repelling the contention that Mohammad Ali, respondent No. 1, is a bonafide purchaser for valuable consideration and Ayat Steels Ltd having purchased from Capital Ship Breakers cannot restrain Mohammad Ali. MrBhuiyan submits that in the present suit Ayat Steels Ltd has specifically asserted that they are bonafide purchaser for valuable consideration without notice of the earlier contract or mortgage with Islami Bank by his vendor since Ayat Steels Ltd had pursued due care before its purchase as it requires as per the maxim of "Caveat Emptor" Ayat Steels Ltd. searched registration office and the Registrar of Joint Stock Companies but found no charge of mortgage, registered. Therefore, principle upon which section 26 clause (b) of the Specific Relief Act has been enacted is a protection for subsequent purchaser who has paid good money on good faith without knowledge of the earlier contract.

18. Mr Bhuiyan, also pointed out that the loan obtained by deposit of title deed is dated 4-11-91 which discloses that it is a security for loan already given and the plaint in the Artha Rin Suit was that the composite loan was sanctioned by letter dated 18-5-91 and there was no mention of any loan given prior to that. Narrating all these facts Mr Bhuiyan submits that the Artha Rin Suit for enforcement of mortgage by depositing title deeds in also barred by limitation and it has no cause of action. Disclosing the statement made in the memorandum of title deeds Mr Bhuiyan submits that the same is hit by section 29 of the Contract Act to render the same void.

19. Lastly. Mr Bhuiyan submits that the question of balance of convenience and inconvenience is very much in favour of the appellant under the facts and circumstances of the case and against the respondent No. 1. therefore, the trial Court ought to have granted injunction in favour of the appellant and a contrary view is not sustainable in law.

20. On the other hand, Mr Mahmudul Islam, the learned Counsel appearing for the respondent Nos. 1-3 having pointed out the fact narrated as above submits. that Capital Ship Breakers having failed in several attempts fighting against the bank in different proceedings like Writ Petitions. Leave Petitions and all that. finally finding no other alternative sold the mortgaged property to the appellant Ayat Steels Ltd on 13-12-2010 while the sale in favour of the respondent No. 1 was confirmed on 23-6-09 and sale certificate was issued and was registered on 25-11-2009, therefore, it is evident that Capital Ship Breakers sold the mortgaged property in favour of Ayat Steels Ltd at a stage when Capital Ship Breakers had no saleable interest at all and after such purchase the appellant as plaintiff instituted Other Class Suit No.3 of 2010 for declaration of title and confirmation of possession on 4-1-2010 and upon institution of the suit a separate application for temporary injunction was also filed by the plaintiff appellant praying for restraining the opposite party i.e. respondent in this appeal from taking possession but after hearing both sides the learned Joint District Judge refused the prayer for injunction which has given rise to this appeal.

21. Mr Mahmudul Islam, referring to the facts disclosed in this appeal submits that this case is a clear manifestation of malafide activities perpetrated by Capital Ship Breakers in which the present appellant has joined, therefore, the appellant is not entitled to any equitable relief.

22. Replying to the submissions made by the learned Counsel for the appellant that an equitable mortgage by memorandum of title deeds cannot be effected in respect of rural property. Mr. Islam submits that such a plea is untenable in law and for the purpose of clarification of such a position Mr Islam pointed out that the territorial restriction referred to in clause (f) of section 58 of Transfer of Property Act has reference to the delivery of deeds only and not to the situation of the property and even if the property situate in the rural area a valid mortgage is created if the delivery of title deeds is made in the towns specified. To substantiate his submission to that effect Mr Mahmudul Islam refers to page 537 of Transfer of Property Act, 6th Edition Vol. 2 by Monohar and Chitaly's. To make it clear it is also pointed out by the learned Counsel that the memorandum of title deeds in the instant case show that it was deposited with the bank's office at 105 Agrabad Commercial Area, Chittagong which is situated in the heart of the city of Chittagong and that section 58(f) of the Transfer of Property Act does not require that the property should physically situate within the specified towns but the provision only requires that the property in question in respect of which equitable mortgage ought to be created, the deposit of title deeds takes place in one of the specific town, as such a valid equitable mortgage was created in the instant case.

23. It is also submitted by Mr Islam that even a property situated outside Bangladesh may be mortgaged by depositing title deed in any of the specified town and in this connection Mr lslam refers to the case of Central Bank of India vs Nusswer Wanji AIR 1932 Bom 642, 643, 644 and State Bank to Mysorevs SM Essence Distilleries AIR 1993 Kant 359 Para 18 and 19.

24. Repelling the submissions made on behalf of the appellants to the effect that for a valid mortgage by depositing of title deed there should be some existing loan and no mortgage by depositing of title deed can be created in respect of any loan to be given in future and in substantiating such sub- mission the appellant also referred to the case reported in 17 DLR (SC) 169 and PLD 1969 Kar 123. It is submitted by the learned Counsel for the respondent that none of these decisions supports the proposition advanced by the appellant. These decisions do not state that the mortgage by depositing of title deeds must always be in respect of existing loan.

25. In reply to the submissions advanced on behalf of the appellant that the Artha Rin Suit was barred by limitation as such the decree was void and the auction purchase by the respondent No. I is without any basis. Mr Islam, refers to the plaint paragraph 24 of Artha Rin Suit No. 29 of 2005 where from it is submitted that the statement made in paragraph 24 of the plaint shows that the time of re- payment expired on 31-12-2004. The defendant did not enter appearance and contest the above statement and hence the suit filed on 16-3-2005 was clearly within the period of limitation under Article 132(c) of the Limitation Act which is 12 years. It is also pointed out by the learned Counsel that assuming for argument sake but not conceding that the suit is barred by limitation, even then the decree passed will not be without jurisdiction and, as such, binding on the parties unless it is set aside in appeal particularly in view of section 20 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003.

26. In substantiating his submission the. learned Counsel refers to three cases reported in AIR 1964 SC 907, AIR 1934 Cal 282 and AIR 1932 All 273.

27. It is also submitted by the learned Counsel for the respondent that the defects if any pointed out by the appellant in respect of the said Artha Rin Suit could have been pointed out in the suit itself and such attempt having not been done throughout the proceedings of the suit such plea is now barred by principle of constructive res judicata under section 11 Explanation IV of the Code of Civil Procedure and the issue being res judicata against Capital Ship Breakers are also res judicata against the appellant which is definitely stepping into the shoes of Capital Ship Breakers and for this purpose reliance has been placed in the case reported in 34 DR 418 and AIR 1986 SC 391. It is also pointed out on behalf of the respondent that the Artha Rin Suit have been decreed as early as on 26-6-05 and Capital Ship Breakers having not challenged the decree at all any stage thereafter the decree has attained finality and now the appellant claiming under Capital Ship Breakers cannot assail the validity of the decree.

28. It is also submitted by Mr Islam that assuming for argument sake but not conceding that the decree is barred and auction sale is without any basis what will be the legal consequence? Whether the defects of the decree affect the title of the opposite party No. 1 the auction purchaser? The answer is clearly in the negative. The opposite party No. 1 is clearly a bonafide purchaser for value without notice of any proceeding for setting aside of the decree in which decree can be set aside. In fact there was no proceeding whatsoever except the execution proceeding when opposite party No. 1 auction purchased the property on 17-4-2008. Hence, even if today the decree is set aside it will not affect the validity of auction sale and the title of opposite party No. 1 by virtue of auction purchase. In substantiating such contention Mr Islam refers to the case of Chinna Mal vs Arumuughon AIR 1990 SC 1828 para 10 and II Govinda Raovs Devi Sahay AIR 1982 SC page 989 para 60 and 61.

29. Mr Islam submits lastly that the learned Joint District Judge having applied his judicial mind to the facts and circumstances involved in the suit has correctly arrived at a decision in respect of the prayer for temporary injunction made by the appellant as plaintiff upon refusing the same assigning reasons as such the impugned order calls for no interference by this Court.

30. Heard the learned Counsels appearing from both sides, perused the memorandum of appeal and the impugned orders and the series of affidavits and counter affidavits tiled from both sides where from it transpires that both sides have made an attempt to substantiate their respective claims to the effect that both the appellant and the respondent No. 1 are bonafide purchasers for valuable consideration without notice of the defect of their respective vendors title. But from the facts narrated and disclosed before us it is apparent that the appellant is claiming to have purchased the suit property from Capital Ship Breakers which was a borrower defendant in a previously instituted Altha Rin Suit being Artha Rin Suit No. 29 of 2005 brought by Islami Bank Bangladesh Limited as plaintiff and the said suit was decreed ex parte and eventually the property involved in the memorandum of mortgage by depositing of title deed were sold in auction and the respondent No. 1 as bidder participated in the said auction and eventually succeeded in purchasing the same through Court by a registered consolidated sale deed on 25-11-2009 which is called bainama. The said decree of the Artha Rin Suit was not challenged before any higher forum by the borrower defendant namely Capital Ship Breakers, on the other hand, plaintiff appellant is claiming to have purchased the same property as was involved in the Artha Rin Suit from Capital Ship Breakers by a registered deed of transfer on December 2, 2009 and December 13, 2009 (two sets of executants got the deed registered on 2 dates) while the sale deed was executed by the executants on 30-11-2009.

31. In this connection it should be remembered that we are now dealing with an interlocutory matter like an order of temporary injunction arising out of the main suit and the question raised before this Court by both the parties are matters to be decided by the trial Court on the basis of evidence to be adduced by both sides at the trial but for the purpose of a prima facie case we cannot but look into the facts giving rise to this appeal for this limited purpose. It is also apparent that Capital Ship Breakers had lost in the legal battle with the Islami Bank and the said legal battle was finally settled and was never reopened subsequently by the defeated party, albeit it is apparent that several attempts were made on behalf of the Capital Ship Breakers by bringing out different proceedings in the name of writ petitions where it had lost in this Court and subsequently before higher Court where also they failed. The respondent No. 1 is a auction purchaser through Court where the sale certificate was granted in his favour on 23-6-2009 i.e. earlier than the one acquired by the plaintiff appellant since his claim of purchase was by way of registered deed executed on 30-11-2009.

32. In this backdrop it is apparent that the plaintiff at this stage cannot claim title in the suit land in his favour and if that be so the balance of convenience and inconvenience must also be drawn on the basis of prima facie case disclosed by the parties involved. The claim of acquisition of title by the plaintiff does not appear to be stronger than the one claimed by his adversary in the case, balance of convenience also goes against him.

<u>33. Many decisions cited by the learned Counsels from both sides and we have disclosed all those in the forgoing paragraph of this judgment and have also gone through all those cases where from we are of the considered opinion that the territorial restriction referred to in clause (f) of section 58 of the Transfer of Property Act has a reference to delivery of deeds only and not to the situation of the property mortgaged and even if a property situated in rural area a valid mortgage may be created if the delivery of title deeds is made in any town specified in section 58(f) of the Transfer of Property Act and it does not require the property to be urban property.</u>

34. This property in respect of which equitable mortgage (mortgage by depositing of memorandum of deeds) sought to be created; the deposit of title deeds must take place in one of the specified town.

35. Therefore, the territorial restriction referred to in clause (f) of section 58 does not refer to the situation of the property mortgaged but refers only to the place where such deposit was made or created and even a property situated outside Bangladesh may also be mortgaged by depositing title deeds in any specified town. In this connection reference may be made to the case reported in AIR 1932 642 and AIR 1993 (Kant) 359.

36. Having gone through the cases reported in 17 DLR (SC) 169 and the case reported in PLD 1969 we find that none of these two cases in any way substantiate the submission made by the learned Counsel for the appellant that no mortgage by depositing of title deed can be created for receiving loan in future.

37. Without giving too much stretch on the submissions made by the learned Counsels from both sides on the point of legality or otherwise of the title acquired by the respective parties and keeping the same to be finally decided by the trial Court on the basis of evidence on record, we find that the question raised before us on the facts and circumstances already noted above, the conclusion is that the impugned order refusing the prayer for temporary injunction do not call for any interference by this Court as such we do not find substance in this appeal, accordingly, the same is dismissed without any order as to costs and the connected Civil Rule being CR No. 421 (fm) of 2010 also stands disposed of accordingly.

Send down a Copy of this order to the trial Court, at once.

End.

Md Idrisur Rahman ----- For the Petitioner. 
Md Ziaul Haque ----- For Respondent No.2
parties:
Amir Ali (Md) ------ Petitioner 
vs 
Joint District Judge and Artha Rin Adalat Fourth Court, Dhaka and another ------ Respondents
full_judgment:
Md Tofazzul Islam J : The petitioner filed this writ petition challenging the order dated 25-3-2003 passed by the Joint District Judge and Artha Rin Adalat, 4th Court, Dhaka by which civil warrant of arrest was issued against the, petitioner, fixing the next date on 30-4-2003 for execution and return of warrant.

2. The case of the petitioners is that he applied to the respondent No.2 bank for a loan of Taka 50,00.000 and he, having deposited the margin amount of Taka 15,00,000 was granted in his favour and as security of the above loan, the petitioner made equitable mortgage of his properties and though he made substantial payment the respondent No. 2 filed Title Suit No. 88 of 1993 praying for realisation of Taka 61,69,201 by sale of the mortgaged properties and on.3 1-8-1997 prelim in any decree was passed ordering that in default of the payment of the aforesaid amount of Taka 61,69,201 with interest etc in terms of preliminary, decree final decree was passed on 9-7-1998 and then to enforce the same the respondent No. 2 filed Title Execution Case No. 59 of 1998 praying for, realisation of the decretal amount with cost, interest etc by sale, of the mortgaged properties and subsequently, at the prayer of the respondent No. 2 the Court below attached the properties mortgaged by the petitioner and fixed the date of auction on 2-3-2000 for sale of the attached properties. However, by order dated 19-2-2000 passed in Miscellaneous ease No. 14 of 2000, which was started on the basis of an application filed under Order XXI rule 58 filed by one Rowshan Ara, who claimed ownership on the mortgaged properties, further proceeding of the above execution case Was stayed till disposal of the aforesaid miscellaneous case. Then on 31-3-2003 the aforesaid Miscellaneous case was taken up for hearing and Rowshan Ara, the petitioner of the above Miscellaneous case having not been found on call, the aforesaid Miscellaneous Case was dismissed for default. However in the meantime, on 25-3-2003, on the basis of the application filed by the respondent No.2 under Order XLI, rule 37 Cl'C Annexure-D, praying for issuance of warrant of arrest, against' the petitioner/judgment-debtor, the impugned order, Annexure-D(1), was passed.

3. The respondent No.2 though did not file any affidavit-in-opposition filed two applications one for discharging the Rule and another for vacating the order of stay and the petitioner filed affidavits- in-opposition against both the applications. Since common question of law and facts are involved in both the applications as well as the main writ petition, both the applications as well as main writ petition are disposed of by this single judgment.

4. Mr Md Idrisur Rahman, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner, submits that in the instant case decree was passed for realisation of Taka 61,69,201 along with interest cost etc by way of selling the mortgaged properties and then application for execution was filed under Order XXI, rule 11 (2)CC seeking the assistance of Court only for sale of the mortgaged properties and not for arrest and detention of the petitioner/judgment- debtor in civil prison and moreover, in terms of the provisions of the proviso to section 51 CPC no opportunity was given to the judgment-debtor for showing cause as to why he should not be. committed to civil prison and further in terms of the provisions of Order XXI, rule 37 CPC no notice was given to the judgment-debtor/petitioner asking him to appear before the Court and as held in the case of Antibiotic Stores and others vs Subordinate Judge, Artha Rin Ada/at and others, 55 DLR (AD) 13, in execution proceeding pending before the Artha Rin Adalat, provisions of the Code of Civil Procedure will be applicable and accordingly, the impugned order; having been passed without complying the specific provisions of the Code of Civil Procedure will be applicable and accordingly, the impugned order, having been passed without complying the specific provisions of the Code of Civil Procedure cannot be sustained and the principle laid down in 54 DLR 78 is not applicable in the facts and circumstances of the present case.

5. Mr Md Ziaul Haque, the learned Advocate appearing for respondent No. 2, submits that due to conspiracy of the petitioner/judgment-debtor no bidder turned up on the date fixed for auction and the judgment-debtor/petitioner, with malafide intention, pushed forward his sister Raushan Ara to file the above Miscellaneous Case. No. 24 of 2000 and obtained the order of stay. Further, in terms of Order XXI, rule 30 CPC decree having been passed for payment of money, the Court was to pass order for issuing Civil Warrant for arrest of the judgment- debtor and accordingly, the respondent No. 2 filed application dated 25-2-2003 under Order XXI, rule 37 CPC Annexure-D, in terms of which the impugned order WIlS passed and in the case of Hazera Begum vs Artha Rin Adalat 54 DLR 78 it has been held that under section 6(Ka) of Artha Rin Adalat Ain 1990, as amended, the Artha Rin Adalat has power to pass order for arrest of even a women in execution of a decree for payment of money in spite of the provisions of section 56 CPC which bars issuing order of arrest or detention in the civil prison of a woman in execution of a decree for payment of money and accordingly, since under the above section 6(Ka), Artha Rin Adalat has been given the power even to pass an order which may not be in conformity with the provisions of the Code of Civil Procedure relating to the execution of a decree, no interference with the impugned order is called for.

Heard the learned Advocates.

6. We have perused the contentions of the provisions of section 51 as well as rules 30 and 37 of Order XXI CPC.

Section 51 CPC provides that the Court may order execution of the decree by attachment and sale or by sale without attachment of any property and also by arrest and detention in prison of the judgment-debtor provided that, where the decree is for the payment of money, execution by detention in prison shall not be ordered unless, after giving the judgment-debtor an opportunity of showing cause why he should not be committed to prison, the Court for reasons recorded in writing is also satisfied.

(a) that the judgment-debtor, with the object or effect of obstructing or delaying the execution of the decree.

(i) is likely to abscond or leave the local limits of the jurisdiction of the Court, or

(ii) has, after the institution of the suit in which the decree was passed dishonestly transferred concealed or removed any part of his property, or committed any other act of bad faith in relation to his property, or

(b) that the judgment-debtor has, or has had since the date of the decree the means to pay the amount of the decree or some substantial part thereof and refuses or neglects or has refused or neglected to pay the same, or

(c) that the decree is for a sum for which the judgment-debtor was bound in a fiduciary capacity to account.

Order XXI, rule 37 also provides that where an application is for the execution of a decree for the payment of money by the arrest and detention in the civil prison of a judgment-debtor who is liable to be arrested in pursuance of the application the Court (shall), instead of issuing a warrant for his arrest, issue a notice calling upon him to appear before the Court on a day to be specified in the notice and show cause why he should not be committed to the civil prison.

7. It also appears in terms of Order XXI, rule 30 CPC every decree for the payment of money including a decree for the payment of money as the alternative to some other relief may be executed by the detention in the civil prison of the judgment- debtor, or by the attachment and sale of his properties or by both.

8. From the contents of the applications dated 25-3-2003 Annexure-D, it appears that respondent No.2 Bank filed the present execution case for realisation of Taka 96, 61,374 as on 20-8-1998 with 18% compensation and in the aforesaid application they took the stand that decree was to be executed by way of attachment and sale of the mortgaged properties and also by putting the petitioner/ judgment-debtor in civil prison.

9. However in terms of the proviso to section 51 CPC execution by detention in civil prison shall not be ordered unless the judgment-debtor is given an opportunity to-show cause as to why he should not be committed to prison and the Court is also satisfied about the grounds as provided in clauses (a), (b) and (c) of the proviso to section "51 CPC. Further when an application has been filed under Order XXI, rule 37 CPC execution of a decree for payment of money by the arrest and detention of the judgment-debtor in civil prison, the Court, instead of issuing a warrant of arrest of the judgment-debtor, shall issue a notice calling upon him to appear before the Court on a date to be specified in the notice and show cause why he should not be committed to civil prison unless the Court is satisfied that the judgment-debtor is likely to abscond or leave the local limits of the jurisdiction of the Court.

10. However from the contents of the impugned order, Annexure-D(1) it appears that before passing of the same, no snow cause was issued in terms of the proviso to section 51 CPC and no notice to appear before the Court was issued in . terms of Order XXI, rule 37 CPC and there is also nothing in the impugned order to show that the Court before passing of the same, was satisfied about the grounds as mentioned in clauses (a), (b) and (c) of the proviso to section 51 CPC.

<u>11. In the case of Antibiotic Stores & others vs Subordinate Judge and Artha Rin Adalat and others 55 DLR (AD) 13, the Appellate Division held that under section 5(4) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, Artha Rin Adalat is it Civil Court having all the powers and jurisdiction under the Civil Procedure Code subject to the provision of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain and since the impugned order in question was passed in execution proceeding of the Artha Rin Adalat, the provisions of Code of Civil Procedure should be followed and accordingly, instead of invoking writ jurisdiction it was the duty of the petitioner to avail the procedure laid down in Order XXI, rule 90 CPC in setting aside the auction sale.</u>

12. In the case of Sultana Jute Mills Limited vs Agrani Bank, 46 DLR (AD) 174, the Appellate Division observed as follows:

"Section 5(4) grants 'to the Artha Rin Adalat the powers and jurisdictions of a Civil Court, but subject to the Provisions of the AdaJat Act, section 5(5) makes the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 applicable to the proceeding of the Artha Rin Adalat, but only if the Adalat Act does not contain anything different.

13. In the case of Islami Bank Bangladesh vs Md Shajuddin 52 DLR (AD) 76 it has been held that there being no provision in the Artha Rin contrary to the provision of Order IX, rule 9 CPC Artha Rin Adalat may pass an order restoring a suit which was dismissed for default.

14. Accordingly, in the present execution proceeding while passing the impugned order, Artha Rin Adalat was required to follow the provisions of section 51 and rule 37 of Order XXI CPC regarding issuing show cause notice before passing the impugned order.

15. Regarding section 6(Ka) as it appears the same, merely provides as follows:

ডিক্রি বাস্তবায়ন  Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 (Act V of 1908) এ যাহা কিছুই থাকুক না কেন কোন অর্থ ঋণ আদালতের সিদ্ধান্ত উক্ত আদালত কর্তৃক জারি বাস্তবায়ন করা হইবে।

16. It appears that previously in terms of the provisions of rules 5 to 9 of Order XXI CPC a decree passed. by Artha Rin Adalat had to be transferred to executing Court for execution and as it will appear from the proviso to Order XXI, rule 37 CPC quoted earlier, complication could also arise if the judgment-debtor left the jurisdiction of the executing Court and as it appears it is only to avoid such situation that section 6(Ka) was incorporated in Artha Rin Adalat Ain which gave the Artha Rin Adalat the power to execute the decree passed by it and as it appears the above provision cannot be stretched to imply that in execution cases pending in Artha Rin Adalat the provisions of section 51 and/or Order XXI, rule 37 regarding issue of show cause and other notice etc have been waived.

17. Accordingly, both the applications are dismissed and the rule is made absolute without any order as to costs.

The Court below, however on the basis of application of the decree holder, if any, will be at liberty to issue necessary order for auction sale and/or civil warrant of arrest etc after compliance of the provisions of law.

End.
