full_judgment:
Syed Amirul Islam J : This Rule arises out of an arbitration agreement entered into between the judgment-debtor and the decree-holder-opposite party No.1. The said agreement was executed on 22-6-1987 for laying cable at Mirpur Telephone Exchange and after completion of the work a dispute arose between the parties. It is alleged by the present petitioner and the proforma opposite party Nos. 2 to 4 that the opposite party No. 1 without duly performing the job submitted forged and fictitious bill on account of extra work and in collusion with the dishonest officials of the. petitioner got the same paid. On discovery of the said irregularity the Board has lodged in FIR on 24-4-1989 against the proprietor of the company. In due course the Bureau of Anti-Corruption took up the investigation and seized all the necessary documents from the office of this petitioner. But during the pendency of the criminal case and on refusal of the present petitioner to pay the bill the opposite party No. 1 filed Arbitration Miscellaneous Case No.11 of 1999 against the Bangladesh T&T Board and the opposite party Nos. 2 to 4. Ultimately the Court passed an order under section 20 (1) of the Arbitration Act 1940 appointing Mr Saifuddin, retired Engineer. PWD, as sole Arbitrator by order dated 6-5-1996 and directed the said Arbitrator to submit the award before 30-7-1996. On receipt of said order of appointment of Arbitratorship, the Arbitrator vide notice dated 12- 8-1996 entered into the reference and directed the parties to submit therelevant papers in support of their case, whereupon the opposite party No. 1 in compliance with the same appeared before the Arbitrator. But the present petitioner intimated through a letter to the Arbitrator that it is not possible on their part to participle in the arbitration and file the necessary papers as all the relevant documents have been seized by the Bureau of Anti Corruption in connection with the case started pursuant to the FIR lodged by the Board earlier. It further appears that thereafter the present petitioner did not take part in the arbitration proceeding when the sole Arbitrator ultimately made the award on 10-11-1996 and filed the same before the Court on 11-11-1996 and the Court below made the award rule of the Court by its order dated 18-9-1997 and there- after converting the Arbitration Miscellaneous case No. 11 of 1990 in to Title Suit No. 333 of 1997 and drawn the necessary decree on 20-9-1997. After making of the award a rule of the Court and drawing up the decree the same was put into execution on 21-1-1998 by the opposite party No. 1 through Execution case No.2 of 1998 as the opposite party No. 1 did not comply with the term of the decree within the stipulated time. The opposite party No. 1 filed an application to draw contempt proceeding against the Chairman, Bangladesh Telegraph and Telephone Board (hereinafter called "BTTB") and some of its Directors. The Executing Court issued a show cause notice against the Chairman and order Directors and Officials of the BTTB. The present petitioner filed reply taking a number of grounds and contented that the execution case in it's present form and manner is not maintainable among other as the decree is a nullity in the eye of law. However, that objection was rejected by the Executing Court. Warrant of arrest was issued against the Chairman and other officials of BITB. Being aggrieved by that order dated 24-10-2000 the present petitioner moved his Court in Civil Revision No. 5267 of 2000 and ultimately after hearing the Rule was made absolute and the impugned order dated 24-10-2000 i.e., order of arrest of the officials of the BTTB was set aside and the Executing Court was directed to dispose of the objection on merit and by the impugned order the objection was rejected on a technical ground namely that learned Advocate of the present petitioner and proforma opposite party Nos. 2 to 4 sought adjournment on the ground of engagement in the High Court Division. This Court, however, after hearing the parties by its order dated 11-12-2001 made the Rule absolute and directed the Executing Court to consider the objection raised by the judgment-debtor on merits within two months from the date of receipt of the said order and proceed thereafter in accordance with and by the present impugned order those objections of the present petitioner was rejected by the Executing Court which gave rise to the instant Rule. This is but one part or relevant story.

2. The other relevant part. in short, is that after being notified by the Executing Court the petitioner filed Miscellaneous case No.9 of 1998 contending that the award which was made Rule of the Court on 18-9-1997 is not sustainable in law on various grounds namely that the Arbitrator misconducted the proceeding and misconduct himself in proceeding with the arbitration case without informing the present petitioner and their prayer to stay further proceeding of the arbitration case had been rejected. It is also contended in this Miscellaneous Case No. 9 of 1998 that the award is void ab-initio. Inasmuch as the award was filed by arbitrator in the Court without notifying the present petitioner as has been contemplated by section 14 (1) of the Act. It is also contended that the decree is not sustainable because after tiling of the award by the arbitrator before the Court, the Court did not notify the present petitioner about same pursuant to the provisions of section 20 of the Act in that view of the matter being in the dark about the arbitration proceeding. making and filing of the award in the Court and making the same a rule of the Court, the petitioner was prevented to file any objection under section 33 the Act within the prescribed time of limitation. It is also contended that the award is a nullity in the eye of law as at the relevant time neither the arbitrator nor the Court could pass as award against BTTB as it was a department of the Government inasmuch as the BTTB lost its corporate existence pursuant to Ordinance No. 12 of 1979. This Miscellaneous case on contest was dismissed by the Trial Court vide it's order dated 9-2-1999 where against the petitioner moved this Court in its Revisional and obtained a Rule in Civil Order No. 1664 of 1999 on 16-5-1999 which ultimately was rejected this Court by its order 16-5-1999. Being aggrieved by the aforesaid order of this Court the petitioner filed CPLA No. 352 of 1999 on 3-1-2000 but ultimately that petition was not passed at the time of hearing as a result, that petition was rejected for default. Without pressing the Leave Petition before the Appellate Division of this Court, however, the petitioner filed an application under order 7, rule 11 of the Code for rejecting the plaint on 24-2-2000 and before that the opposite party-decree-holder on 16-1-2000 moved for attachment of bank account of BTTB and the application dated 16-1-2000 was allowed by the Executing Court vide order dated 23-1-2000 and the application filed by the present petitioner under order 7, rule 11 was rejected. The petitioner moved this Court section 115 of the Code which was rejected as CO No. 4160 of 2000 and ultimately on 13-8-2000 the application was not pressed by the petitioner and accordingly it was rejected by this Court as being not pressed.

3. Miscellaneous Case No. 9 of 1998 was rejected on the ground of limitation inasmuch as the petitioner did not raise objection within the period of limitation as contemplated by Article 178 of the Limitation Act.

4. Here it may further be mentioned that against the order of warrant of arrest issued by the Executing Court the aggrieved persons preferred Civil Revision No. 5367 of 2002 and that rule on contest was made absolute on 11-12-2002 and pursuant to the direction given by this Court in the aforesaid Civil Revision, the Executing Court ultimately after considering the objections of the present petitioner rejected the same by the present impugned order which is under challenge before us.

5. Mr Rais Uddin Ahmed, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner submits that the Executing Court committed an error of law occasioning failure of justice in rejecting the objections of the petitioner simply on the ground that the award given by the arbitrator was an ex parte one and the objections which they have now raised before the Executing Court could have been raised before the Trial Court in an application filed under section 33 read with section 30 of the Arbitration Act but since the petitioner did not file any objection whatsoever under section 33 of the Act the trial Court did not commit any illegality in making the award a rule of the Court and this objection cannot now be taken by the judgment-debtor before the Executing Court.

6. Mr Rais Uddin vehemently criticized the observations of the Executing Court and submitted that in passing the impugned order the Executing Court lost sight of the fact that the instant decree is a nullity in the eye of law inasmuch as the arbitration proceeding was initiated by the decree-holder- opposite party No. 1 against the Chairman of BTTB and other officials of the Board when the Board had no corporate existence of its own and became a department of the Government and has lost its right to sue be sued in its name and thus the decree obtained by the decree-holder is a nullity in the eye of law. To fortify his submission he relied on the famous dicta given by Lord Denning in Mac Foy vs United Africa Company Limited (1962) AC 152 and submitted that when the order is void ah initio it is non est and do not have any legal value.

7. Mr Rais Uddin the learned Advocate most empathically submits that if the scheme, scope and purpose of the Arbitration Act is examined, it becomes clear that the arbitration proceeding consists of three stages namely the appointment of the arbitrator either mutually by the parties to the agreement or by the Court and secondly a duty is cast upon the arbitrator to initiate the arbitration proceeding within the time as agreed upon or in the absence of any provisions to the contrary the arbitration must be completed within four months as per Article of the first schedule to the Act and in the instant case the Court by it's order dated 6-5-1996 appointed Mr Saifuddin as Arbitrator and directed him to complete the arbitration proceeding before 30-7-1996, but unfortunately in the instant case the arbitrator not only failed to initiate the arbitration reference within the prescribed time but he did not take any steps to complete the arbitration before the prescribed time and on 12-8-1996 he served notice upon the parties to submit their papers in support of their claim and this assumption of jurisdiction, according to Mr Rais Uddin is absolutely illegal and contrary to ,the provision' of law inasmuch as the arbitrator was under the obligation to close the arbitration proceeding and make the award and submit the same before 30-7-1996. Thereafter, the initiation of the proceeding of the arbitration case well after the expiry of 30-7-1996 is absolutely without jurisdiction, he contends. The learned Advocate further submits that it is only the Court which can extend time for making the award but admitted possession is that the passing of the order dated 6-5-1996 till the date of filing of the award on 11-11-1996 at no stage of the proceeding the time was ever extended by the Court for making and filing of the award in the Court.

8. Mr Rais Uddin, the learned Advocate to substantiate his contention relies on the order No. 65 and 66 of dated 16-9-1966 and 22-9-1966 respectively and submits that even if for argument sake it is admitted that on 16-9-1996 the Court refused the application dated 12-9-1996 filed by the arbitrator for extending the time for filing of the award then also instant award is a nullity inasmuch as from the order No. 66 dated 22-9-1996 it appears that Court extended the time till 16-11-1996 for filing of the award "(award dakhil)". Referring to the words "Award dakhil" in the said order, Mr Rais Uddin submits that this order clearly indicates that by his application dated 12-9-1996 filed before the Court the 'arbitrator applied for extension of time for filing of the award but there is no provision in the Act which empowers the Court to extend time for filing of the award. Therefore, the dated 22-9-1996 has no legal value and this order cannot be cured as patent illegally has been committed by the arbitrator in applying for extension of time for making the award and since no extension was ever taken by the parties for making the award on this account also the award is a nullity in the eye of law.

9. Mr Rais Uddin further contended that from the materials on record and the' award itself it is obvious on the face of the record that no notice either under section 14(1) of the Act ever served upon the petitioner which prevented the petitioner from availing of their valuable right given to a party to the arbitration agreement by section 33 of the Act and the non compliance with section 14(1) and (2) also renders the instant award a nullity. Mr Rais Uddin, in this connection relied on an unreported decision of this Court given in the case of Chief Engineer; Roads and Highway, Government of the People s Republic of Bangladesh vs Messrs Concord Engineering Construction i.e., FMA No, 82 of 1993 wherein this Court by delivering judgment on 4-4-1996 observed that a duty cast upon the Court to examine the legality or validity of the award before making the same a rule of the Court under section 17 of the Act even in the absence of any objection raised by a party against the award under section 33 read with section 30 or section 16 read with section 33 of the Act. He then, submits that the High Court Division judgment was appealed against in the Appellate Division and in the Appellate Division it was registered in CA No. 9 of 2001 and the Appellate Division by their judgment dated 3-8-2004 dismissed the appeal and did not find anything to interfere with the observation given by this Court on this aspect. He, therefore, relying on this decision submits that the legal position is clear that no matter whether a party to the arbitration agreement raises any objection or not as to the legality or otherwise of an award nevertheless a duty is imposed upon the Court to examine the legal aspect of the case and if it is found that the award is according of law then only it will make the award a rule of the Court. but unfortunately in the instant case the learned Court below in making the award rule of the Court lost sight of this aspect of the case and made the award a rule of the Court simply on the ground that the present did not file objection against award within specified 30 days and hence the Court made the award a rule of the Court. On this point Mr Rais Uddin, further argued that legal position is clear and there cannot be waiver or estoppels against law. In the facts and circumstances of the case Executing Court is also under legal obligation to see if the instant decree is executable or not and to see that this Court is also entitled to examine the legality or validity of the decree in question. Mr Rais Uddin submitted that no doubt this rule arises out of an order passed by the Executing Court in Executing case No.2 of 1996 at a point of time when section 47 of the Code is no more there but nevertheless in the interest of justice an Executing Court is under the legal objection to see if the decree put into execution is in fact executable or not or in other words if it stands the security of law and in the instant case a perusal of the decree would lead us to the conclusion that the arbitrator most illegally assumed jurisdiction to arbitrate the dispute and made the award beyond time without any lawful authority which renders the decree a nullity in the eye of law. Mr Rais Uddin also on the point of nullity submitted that the arbitration proceeding as well as the execution case was started against BTTB which in fact is a department of the Government and not a corporate body and with the promulgation of Ordinance 12 of 1979 on and from 27-2-1979 the Board lost its corporate existence and became a department of the Government. Thereafter, it has lost its entity to sue or be sued on its own name and in that view of the matter also instant execution case is not maintain- able and in support of his contention he relied on a decision reported in 4BLC (AD) 216. Mr Rais Uddin further submits that an objection had been filed in the execution case by the BTTB as a Government department on behalf of the Government and that the opposite party No. 1 is also pursuing their remedy against the Board and wanted to attach lands of Khatian No. 1 which is belonging to the People's Republic of Bangladesh. Therefore, in the execution case the opposite party No. 1 is pursuing its remedy against the Government of Bangladesh but Bangladesh is not a party to that arbitration agreement and the award is also not against the Government and on that ground also the proceeding of the execution case ought to have been stopped by the Court below. Mr Rais Uddin further submits that since the opposite party No.2 pursuing their remedy against the Government and/or Government Officials in their official capacity then also the decree in question is not executable as the provision of section 82 of the Code has not been followed and a cursory view of the record of the execution case clearly indicates that the executing Court did not pay any heed to the provision of section 82 of the code and the violation of which also renders the execution proceeding a nullity. Mr Rais Uddin then attacks the award on the ground that the arbitrator has no authority in law to give interest in view of the terms of the agreement but in the instant in the case it is seen that the arbitrator has given interest to the opposite party No. I for the pre-reference period, for the period under reference and for the period till the realization of the amount and therefore he contends that on this account also the award has no legs to stand upon as it is contrary to provision of law as contained in section 29 of the Act and this vital and material legal aspect of the case was also overlooked by the executing Court in proceeding with the instant execution case.

10. Mr A Y Masihuzzaman, the learned Advocate appearing for the decree-holder-opposite party, on the other hand, makes a straight forward submission. His first contention is that the instant rule has arisen out of an execution proceeding and it is now well settled that a Executing Court cannot go beyond the decree and therefore all the legal questions that have been raised by the petitioner in this Court could be a valid ground for an application filed under section 33 of the Act but. there is no scope for the petitioner to raise these questions in the instant proceeding as the Court cannot go beyond the decree. In support of his contention he relied on the decision reported in AIR 1970 SC and 28 DLR (AD) 57. He then submits that the admitted position is that the Order dated 6-5-1996 was passed in Arbitration Miscellaneous Case No. 11 of 1990 wherein the present petitioner entered appearance and contested the application for appointing an arbitrator and admittedly after filing of the award on 16-11-1996 the petitioner for reasons best known to them did not file any objection either under section. 16 and/or under section 33 of this Act and in that circumstance the Court below had no other alternative but to make the award rule of the Court after the expiry of the 30 days from the date of filing of the award and by making the award a rule of the Court in the facts and circumstances of the case the Court below did not commit any illegally whatsoever. The learned Advocate further submits that it is also now well settled that omission to notify the parties about the signing of the award and filing of the same in the Court is mere irregularity and not an illegality and thus the merit of the award is not affected in any way thereby. Therefore, in the instant case non service of notices upon the parties about the making and signing of the award and/or filing of the same in the Court is immaterial and cannot have any bearing upon the merits of the decree. To meet the argument of Mr Rais Uddin on the point of interest Mr Masihuzzaman subm itted that section 29 of the Act has been interpreted a number of cases by our Appellate Division and it is now well settled that the arbitrator is empowered to award interest beyond the reference period and can also give interest for the pre-reference period if so provided by the agreement and claimed by the party and in support of his contention he relied on the decision reported in 46 DLR (AD) 96 and on this point Mr Masihuzzarnan frankly concedes that in any case it is the discretion of the Court to give the interest for the period beyond time from the date of award till the date of realization of the amount, therefore mere passing an order for interest either for the pre-reference period or for the post reference period does not render the award a nullity.

11.Mr Masihuzzaman then raises an important question as to the maintainability of this application. His first submission is that the instant rule is not maintainable in its present form as the Chairman of BTTB has represented Bangladesh but the Government of Bangladesh is represented by it's appropriate Secretary which is absent in the present case and therefore this rule suffers from patent infirmity and is liable to be rejected as misconceived and incompetent one. On this point Mr Masihuzzaman rises a furthe question which is the doctrine of principle of res-judicata. Mr Masihuzzaman submits admittedly the petitioner participated in Arbitration Miscellaneous Case No. 11 of 1990 and after of Miscellaneous Execution Case No.2 of 1998 they filed Arbitration Miscellaneous Case No.9 of 1998 in the Court below which was dismissed and against both the judgments they moved this Court unsuccessfully whereupon they filed Special Leave to Appeal before the Appellate Division and that application was also dismissed for default as that was not pressed before the Appellate Division and on top or that in the execution case itself the present petitioner has filed an application under Order 7, rule 11 of the Code which on contest was rejected by the Court below against which they moved this Court under section 115(1) of the Code and obtained a rule in Civil Revision No. 4160 of 2000 and that rule was also ultimately rejected as not being pressed and the present petitioner has tiled an objection before the Executing Court which is liable to be rejected as the petitioner is guilty of committing fraud upon the Court as by suppressing the aforesaid facts the petitioner obtained the rule and after drawing of the decree the present petitioner cannot re-agitate the points which they had agitated in Miscellaneous Case No.9 of 1998 and thus the present objection is caught by the mischief of principle of res-judicata.

12. Mr Masihuzzaman has filed supplementary affidavit on behalf of the opposite party No. 1 on 20-1-2005 wherein Order Nos. 65 and 66 of Arbitration Miscellaneous Case No. 11 of 1990 has been annexed as Annexure- 'M' to the affidavit. Referring to the aforesaid orders he submits that the arbitrator wrote a letter on 12-9-1996 to the Court for extension of time which was kept with the record on 16-9-1996 and passed the necessary order on 20-9-1996 whereby the time was extended till 16-11-1996 for filing of the award and admittedly on 11-11-1996 the award was filed by the arbitrator before the Court therefore on this Count also the award stands the scrutiny of law. To meet the argument of Mr Rais Uddin that the execution case cannot proceed against the parties, he submits that in the Arbitration Miscellaneous Case No. 11 of 1990 BTTB is represented by it's Chairman and contested the case and they also participated in the arbitration proceeding by writing a letter on 12-9-1996 informing the arbitrator that they are unable to file the relevant documents before him as the same has been seized by the investigating officer of the Bureau of Anti Corruption and then also filed Miscellaneous Case No.9 of 1998 by the BTTB represented by its Chair- man and it is only in the execution case for the first time raised the question that BTTB has lost its corporate existence on the strength of the decision reported in 4 BLC (AD) 216 but before that the BTTB has contested the case in its own name. Therefore, in the instant case the petitioner is caught by the doctrine of estoppel.

13. We have perused the application, counter affidavit, number of supplementary affidavits filed by both the parties and perused the papers as annexed therewith. On a perusal of the award and the papers annexed with this rule, it appears that there is no dispute between the parties that BTTB entered into an agreement with the opposite party No. 1 for laying cable line in Mirpur in the city of Dhaka and that agreement also contains a clause for arbitration. The admitted possession is that the opposite party No.2 filed an application under section 20(1) of the Act for appointment of an arbitrator by the Court which was registered as Arbitration Miscellaneous Case No. 11 of 1990 and the proceeding of the said case was stayed for some time and ultimately by order dated 6-5-1996 the Court below appointed an arbitrator and directed him to submit the award before 30-7-1996. The further admitted position is that the arbitrator entered into reference by serving a notice upon the parties on 12- 8-1996 and ultimately made and signed the award on 10-11-1996 and submitted the same before the Court on 11-11-1996 and time for filing of the award was extended at the instance of the arbitrator till 16-11-1996.

14. The opposite party No. 1 did not take the ground of locus standi in the counter affidavit. The legal position is that with the promulgation of Ordinance 12 of 1979 no suit or other legal proceedings would lie against the Board as a corporate body but from the materials on record namely the record of Arbitration Miscellaneous Case No. 11 of 1990 and Miscellaneous Case No.9 of 1996, it appears that the Board also treated itself as a body corporate. It further appears that even after the coming into force the Ordinance No. 12 of 1979 the Board retained its original name. But the Appellate Division in the case reported in 4 BLC (AD) 216 has held that with the promulgation of the Ordinance BTTB become a Government Department and hence Board could no longer sue or be sued in its own name and relying on this decision and the provision of Ordinance No. 12 of 1979 the present petitioner most empathically argued that the decree obtained by the opposite party No. 1 is a nullity in the eye of law inasmuch as the entire proceeding was a nullity because of the fact that it was instituted against an authority which is non existent in the eye of law.

1<u>5. We think that it would be better to decide this issue of locus standi of the petitioner first. Now let us see which of the two conflicting submissions is sustainable. We have examined the provisions of Ordinance 12 of 1979 and it appears that it was promulgated on 27th February, 1979 after repealing the T&T Board Ordinance, 1975 with certain savings. It further appears that with the promulgation of the said Ordinance BTTB become with effect from the 27th February, 1979 a department of Government and it lost its corporate existence. Inspite of that it appears that the tender was floated in 1987 and the parties entered into an agreement pursuant to that tender on 22-6-1987 wherein the BTTB represented it as a body corporate without realizing its' legal position and the decree-holder also entered into agreement with them in that capacity. The further admitted possession is that Arbitration Miscellaneous Case No. 11 of 1990 was initiated against the Board as an Autonomous Body and in that case also the BTTB contested the same as a corporate body. So, there is no denying of the fact until they filed an application in the execution case, the BTTB treated it as an Autonomous Body. The opposite party No. 1 also pursued their claim against the BTTB all through without realizing about the legal status of the present petitioner. It is only in the Execution case the petitioner filed an application stating clearly that the legal position has changed. But from the records of the execution case i.e. execution application and the counter affidavit of this rule, it appears that the opposite party No. 1 in the execution case made a prayer of attachment of Government properties and from the contention of the counter affidavit it also appears that they pursuing their remedy against the Government of the People's Republic of Bangladesh by suing its department namely BTTB. There are overwhelming material on record to show that the opposite party No. 1 acted relying on the representation made by the present petitioner as Bangladesh T &T . Board represented by its Chairman without disclosing further as to whether it is an autonomous body or itself a department of the Government. But fact remains that from 27th February, 1979 the BTTB lost its corporate character and became a Government department pursuant to the provisions of Ordinance No. 12 of 1979. It appears that both the parties being in the dark about the status of BTTB pursuing each other without practically disclosing the real character of the present petitioner, So, it is established beyond doubt that even the BTTB when entered into the contract with the opposite party did riot realize that they are no more an autonomous body and has become a department of the Government. In these circumstances does it lie in the mouth of BTTB to say that the proceeding initiated against BTTB as an autonomous body is a nullity or BTTB is stopped by the doctrine of estoppel? We think that the doctrine of estoppel cannot be pressed into service for the simple reason that there cannot be any estoppel against law. No doubt, the opposite party was misled by the then BTTB about its legal character but ignorance of law cannot be a ground for seeking relief. It further appears that the opposite party sought its relief against the government but unfortunately without impleading the People's Republic of Bangladesh as a party either before the arbitrator or before the Court below. Thus, the opposite party pursued its claim against a non-existent entity. Therefore, the award as well as the decree seems to be absolutely a nullity.</u>

16. It has been canvassed by Mr Masihuzzaman that present revisional application is not maintain- able because it has been filed by Bangladesh represented by the Chairman, BTTB which is against the rule of business by the Government and if, in fact. Bangladesh would be the applicant then Bangladesh ought to have been represented by the appropriate Secretary of Bangladesh. From the materials on record i.e. cause title of the instant revisional application and the power executed by the petitioner it becomes clear that in the instant case Bangladesh is represented by the Chairman of BTTB. No doubt generally Bangladesh is represented in the Courts of law either by the Deputy Commissioner or by the Secretary but when a proceeding is initiated by a citizen against department of the Government on many occasion the Government is represented by the department and in the instant case admittedly BTTB became a Government department in 1979 and the opposite party No. 1 is pursuing its relief against the said Board. In the instant case the Chairman as the chief executive of the department is representing the Government as is evident from the relevant papers. There are many examples where in a litigation a government department is represented by government officials. We have been referred to an unreported decision given in FMA No. 82 of 1993 and in that case it is seen that the Public Works Department of the Government was represented by the Chief Engineer, Roads and Highways and not by the Secretary, Ministry of the Works. When there arc litigations arising out of commercial activities of the Government usually the concerned officials represent the Government. Therefore, we find that the instant application is maintainable inasmuch as a Government Department is represented by its Chairman, the highest official of the department.

17. We have earlier noted the various points urged before us by the learned Advocates for the parties. We think that of the remaining questions we should now divert our attention to the contention raised by Mr Rais Uddin as to whether the award is a nullity. We want to advert to this question now because if the contention is accepted in that case we would not be required to advert to the other points raised by the parties. Mr Rais Uddin relying on various fact and circumstances submitted that the award in question and the decree drawn on the basis of an illegal award is also a nullity because the arbitrator entered into the reference at a point of time when his authority to initiate the arbitration proceeding ceased. The admitted position is that pursuant to the Court's order passed in Arbitration Miscellaneous Case No. 11 of 1990 dated 6-5-1996 Mr Saifuddin was appointed as an arbitrator and he was directed to submit the award before 30-7-1996. The further admitted position is that his jurisdiction expired on 30-7-1996. The arbitrator for the first time served notice upon the parties on 12-8-1996 asking them to submit all the relevant papers to support their respective cases. On receipt of the said letter the present petitioner vide their letter dated 26-9- 1996 informed the arbitrator that all the relevant papers in connection with the job has been seized by the Bureau of Anti-Corruption in connection with Criminal-Case filed against the opposite party No.1 and in that view of the matter it would not be possible on their part to file the documents and therefore they prayed for staying all further proceedings of the arbitration. Till the date of filing of the award in the Court at no point of time the arbitrator intimated the petitioner that prayer of the present petitioner was refused and that he would preceed with the arbitration proceeding ex parte. The arbitrator ultimately passed an ex parte award on 10-11-1996. In view of these admitted facts Mr Rais Uddin submitted that in order to appreciate the scope of the law and the scheme of the Act the provisions of section 28 of the Act should be looked into. He submitted that an arbitration proceeding consists of three different stages after the appointment of an arbitrator. Entering into the reference by the arbitrator i.e. when he calls upon the parties to appear before him to submit their case and the second stage is making and signing of the award and final stage is filing of the award before the competent Court. In the instant case the proceeding was ex-parte and behind the back of the present petitioner. Further admitted position is that at no point of time till 11-11-1996 the arbitrator ever applied to the Court for extension of time for making the award and the Order No. 65 dated 16-9-1996 which has been annexed by the opposite party No. 1 shows that the arbitrator sent a letter dated 12-9-1996 to the Court and on the application of the opposite party dated 16-9-1996 the Court below vide order dated 16-9-1996 passed an order to keep the said application of the arbitrator with the record. Subsequently vide order dated 22-9-1996 extended the time till 16-11-1996 for filing of the award. From the records, it appears that the award was signed on 10-11-1996 and submitted it before the Court on 11-11-1996. Therefore, it appears that the initiation of the arbitration proceeding by the arbitrator by severing notice on 12-8-1996 is absolutely illegal and without jurisdiction inasmuch as at that point of time he had no legal authority to initiate any arbitration proceeding with- out getting the time extended by the as Courts of ready on 13-7-1996 the time framed given by the Court had expired and this aspect is admitted.

18. We have carefully examined the scheme and the different provisions of the Act and it appears to us that section 28 of the Ordinance empowers the Court to extend time for making the award and there is no dispute that making of the award and filing of the award is not one and same, these are different actions. The admitted position is that the arbitrator had at no point of time till the filing of the award ever applied for extension of time either for initiating the arbitration proceeding after expiry of 30-7-1996 nor applied for extension of time for making the award and this legal aspect of the case has been unfortunately overlooked by the Court below when it made the award rule of the Court. On a critical examination of the provisions of the Act, it appears that there is difference between filing and making of award. The scheme of the Act shows that Court has no authority whatsoever to extend time for filing of the award at the instance of the arbitrator. The Court is only authorized to extend time from time to time for making of the award if for some reason the arbitrator: is unable to make the award within the stipulated time. The Act does contain any provision empowering the Court to extend time for filing of the award because this aspect is covered by Article 178 of the Limitation Act and it appears that even the Court cannot compel the arbitrator to fill the award after making and signing of the same. It is only after of the expiry of three years from the date of making and filing of the award a party to the arbitration proceedings can apply to the Court for directing the arbitrator to send the award as already three years' time has expired. On the other hand, the Court is only empower to extend time for making of the award on sufficient ground at the instance of a patty. From the Order Nos. 65 and 66, it appears that the petitioner only applied for keeping the award with the record and that prayer was allowed by the Court. But it appears to us that Court had no legal power at all to do so because admittedly the award was filed on 11-11-1996. Thus, it appears that the initiation of the proceeding and making of the award beyond the stipulated period of 30-07-1996 is absolutely illegal and without jurisdiction and on that account the award in question. Also is a nullity i.e. void ab-initio and has no existence of its own in the eye of law. Besides, yet on another Court the making of the award rule of the Court is illegal. Section 23 of the Act clearly and unmistakably indicates that when a Court passed an order for arbitration proceeding under section 20 of the Act to adjudicate upon the dispute between the parties, the Court shall spell out in the order that the arbitrator must the award within a given time as is deemed reasonable in the facts and circumstances of the case. In the instant case in passing the order dated 06.05-1996 keeping in view the provision of section 20 of the Act the Court directed the arbitrator to submit the award before 30-07-1996.

19. The admitted position is that the arbitrator did not given any notice to the parties after milking of the award and it is contended by the petitioner that even after filing of the award in the Court on 11-11-1996 the Court below made the award rule of the Court even without notifying the present petitioner. The opposite party No. 1 could not refute this contention. In that view of the factual aspect making of the award a rule of the Court keeping the petitioner in the dark and depriving the petitioner of the most valuable right that has been conferred on them by' section 33 of the Act is manifestly illegal and without jurisdiction.

20. Now it calls for determination if the impugned order is caught by the mischief of doctrine of res-judicata and/or the executing Court can go beyond the decree. To cross the hurdle of res- judicata Mr Rais Uddin relied on the unreported decision of this Court given in the case of the Chief Engineer, Roads and Highway Department, Government of the People's Republic of Bangladesh vs Messrs Concord International and Construction Limited i.e. FMA No. 82 of 1993 which was dis- posed of by the judgment dated 4-4-1996. In that case also the same question Came up for consideration before a Bench of this Court wherein one of us was a party. In that case no objection under section 33 of the Act was filed but in the appeal for the first time the question of validity of the award was raised. So, in that case it was contended by the respondent that the appellant at this belated stage cannot call in question the legality or validity of the award. But Court answered the question in the affirmative. It observed, "In that view of the matter it was bounden duty of the learned Subordinate Judge to suo motu inquire as to the validity or legality of the award before making the same rule of the Curt because jurisdiction goes at the root".

<u>21. Thus, the settled legal proposition is that where. an award is illegal and void for want of jurisdiction apparent on the face of it, it is not necessary that the parties should file objection to the award within the time prescribed under Article 158 of the Limitation Act. We have already discussed the relevant aspects of the case. From the materials on record it is found that the arbitrator assumed- the jurisdiction and entered into reference at a point when he had no mandate to do so. The entire proceeding is vitiated for want of jurisdiction and consequently the award is a nullity. An award which is a nullity in the eye of law cannot be made a rule of the. Court and, as such, the impugned decree is also void ab-initio, This aspect of the case was completely lost sight of by the Court below in making the award rule of the Court. The Court below made the award rule of the Court simply on the ground that no objection was filed by the, present petitioner before him under section 33 of the Act. But the statute is there and the Court was bound to take judicial notice of it. It is not necessary that the party should file objection to the award under section 30 read with section 33 of the Act within the time prescribed under Article 158 of the Limitation Act. In that view of the matter it was the legal obligation of the Court below to suo motu examine the legal position and see if the award is a valid one or not. The fate of the award depends on the legality or validity of the appointment of the arbitrator. It is found that the arbitrator has not assumed jurisdiction as per law and thus the award given by him is void ab-initio and a nullity in the eye of law. The legal incidence of a void act has been succinctly by Lord Denning, MR in Mac Foy vs United Africa Co Ltd (1962) AC 152, 160, "If an act is void, then it is in law a nullity. It is not only bad, but incurably bad. There is no need for an order of the Court to set it aside; It is automatically null and void without more ado, though it is sometimes convenient to have the Court declare it to be so. An every proceeding which is founded on it is also bad incurably bad; you cannot put something on nothing and expect it to stay there. It will collapse. But if an act is only voidable, then it is not automatically void. It is only an irregularity which may be waived; it is not to be avoided unless something is done to avoid it. There must be an order of the Court setting it aside and the Court has discretion whether to set it aside or not. It will do so if justice demands it but not otherwise".</u>

<u>22. A mere reading of the award shows that the arbitrator initiated the proceeding pursuant to the Court's order dated 6-5-1996 but he had assumed the jurisdiction on 11-8-1996 when the time frame given by the Court had expired and the arbitrator had no lawful authority to initiate the proceeding and Court also lost sight of the fact that without get- ting the time extend for making the award the arbitrator made the award and signed it on 10-11-1996. Therefore, we are of the opinion that in making the award rule of the Court the Court acted beyond its jurisdiction and failed to discharge the duty cast upon it by section 17 of the Act. The view taken by us gets further support from the un-reported decision given in the FMA No. 82 of 1993 and also from the decisions reported in 6 DLR 473, ILR 13 (Allahabad) 30, 8 DLR 307.</u>

23. Admittedly this rule arises out of Execution Case No.2 of 1998. Mr Masihuzzaman, the learned Advocate for the opposite party submitted that the Executing Court cannot go beyond the decree. On the other hand, Mr Rais Uddin submitted that the Executing. Court while executing a decree can see if the decree is passed by the competent Court or is a nullity or is without jurisdiction and if it is found to be so the executing Court will refuse to execute the same. We have studied the decisions relied on by Mr Masihuzzaman but it appears that they do not, in fact, support him rather they supported the petitioner. Be that as it may, the legal position is that the executing Court can see if the decree is a nullity or is of without jurisdiction. We have already found that the decree is a nullity, therefore, it is non est and not executable. This aspect of the case not considered by the executing Court. Besides, in view of our aforesaid discussions it is crystal clear that the doctrine of res-judicata as well as the doctrine of estop" pel by judgment have no manner of application to the instant case.

24. Now the question is, whether the doctrine of estoppel will be attracted in the facts and circumstances of the case. The doctrine of estoppel comes into operation when there is a valid decree but when the decree itself is found to be a nullity then the question of application of the doctrine of the nullity does not come into play.

25. Besides, it further appears to us that in the instant case the doctrine of estoppel cannot be pressed into service because of the fact that by initiating the execution case the decree-holder has put into execution a decree which has no existence at all. Therefore, we do not find any substance in the submission of Mr Masihuzzaman in that regard.

26. Since it is found by us that the instant decree is void ab-initio and, as such, a nullity in the eye of law this goes to the root of the case and render the decree a nullity in the eye of law which, therefore, cannot be executed by any Court and in that view of the matter it would be waste of time to advert to other issues by the parties.

27. In the result, the Rule is made absolute. The impugned judgment and order dated 13-6-2002 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, First Court, Dhaka in Title Execution Case No.2 of 1998 is set aside. And since the decree is a nullity there remains nothing to proceed with the Execution case No.2 of 1998.

Send down the Lower Court records at once.

End.

full_judgment:
Md Ashfaqul Islam J: This appeal at the instance of the plaintiff Agrani Bank is directed against the judgment and decree dated 6-11-90 and 12-11-90 respectively passed by the learned Subordinate Judge, Dhaka in Title Suit No. 17 of 1988 without awarding interest pendente lite as well as interest accumulated till the realisation of installments.

2. On 23rd January 1988 appellant Agrani Bank as plaintiff instituted Title Suit No. 17 of 1988 before the Subordinate Judge Dhaka against the respondents for recovery of money after selling the property mortgaged with the plaintiff Bank.

3. Plaint case, in short, is that plaintiff-bank on 30-4-84 advanced a loan facility by an overdraft of Taka 8 lac in favour of defendant-respondent No. 1, Orbit Enterprise Ltd represented by its managing director respondent No.2. The defendant-respondent No.2 mortgaged the property mentioned in schedule of the plaint with the bank for the purpose of securing payment of said loan but subsequently, as the defendant failed to repay the accumulated loan of Taka 8,15,671.65 plaintiff-bank was constrained to file the suit for realisation of the loan money. The total outstanding upto 11-1-88 was calculated at Taka 9,18,219.65. Hence is the suit.

4. The defendant-respondent filed written statement and contested the suit. His case is that after getting a work order to establish electric connection and sanitary works of a building of Bangladesh T &T Board, the plaintiff-bank allowed him the said loan facility. It is further stated in the written statement that after some progress of the work, a dispute cropped up between the defendant- respondent No. 2 and the T &T Board which was ultimately referred to the Arbitration Council. The arbitration council passed an award of Taka 56,78,761 in favour of the respondent and on 30-9- 87 the said award was put to make Rule of the Court before the First Court of Subordinate Judge, Dhaka by Arbitration Miscellaneous Case No. 100 of 1987. In paragraph 'Uma' of the written statement, the defendant No. 1 categorically stated that within few months' time that the said amount would be realised. In the written statement defendant No.1 admitted the entire liability to be discharged against the plaintiffs claim.

5. Upon the above pleadings 3 issues were framed. The plaintiff did not cite any witness and the defendant No. 2 was cited as only defendant witness in the case. The learned Subordinate Judge decreed the suit but did not award the pendente lite interest as prayed by the plaintiff against which this appeal has been preferred by the plaintiff-appellant.

6. Mr SA Rahim appearing with Mr Syed Abdus Salam, the learned Counsel appearing on behalf of the appellant, after taking us through the plaint, written statement, evidence of DW and different exhibits from the record, contends that the learned Subordinate Judge committed an error of law in passing the decree without awarding any interest pendente lite in his decree as well as interest till the realisation of installments in two years. Elaborating his submission, the learned Counsel further contends that though the provision of awarding interest under law is a discretionary one but under the facts and circumstances of the present case the learned Court should have awarded the interest as prayed by the plaintiff in the plaint. He also empathically submits that the learned Court below had ample power to pass the decree with interest pendente lite but it failed to consider to pay the decretal with interest pendente lite amount in one installment and thereby committed illegality.

7. Be that as it may, we have heard the learned Counsel appearing on behalf of the plaintiff- appellant at length and also gone through the plaint, written statement, deposition of DW 1 and other exhibits carefully. The moot question that falls for consideration by this Division in the instant appeal is, whether the subordinate judge was justified in passing the decree appealed against under the facts and circumstances of the present case.

8. In the written statement filed on 16-1-90, it has been categorically stated in paragraph 'Ulna" that the respondent (defendant No.1) is expecting to have the Rule of the Court at any time and in his deposition made before the Court on 5-11-90, the defendant, while admitting the loan categorically stated in his chief আমি আরবিট্রেশন করিয়া সাতান্ন লাখ টাকার বেশী পাই. In his cross-examination, he directly admitted the claim of the plaintiff and prayed for soft installments and also exonerating the interest. lf we analyse the two things i.e. the statement given by the defendant in the written statement and his subsequent deposition, it becomes clear that though the defendant got the amount of Taka 57 lac by way of arbitration from T &T Board still he did not repay the loan amount which is only Taka 9,18,219.65. Therefore, we may glean that by not taking into account this aspect of fact, the Court below certainly flouted the settled proposition of law that discretion should be exercised judiciously and not capriciously. This is indeed, a fit case where the court should have awarded interest at a reasonable rate.

9. It would be profitable in this respect to go through the provision of law which governs the issue before us. Section 34(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure reads as follows:

"34(1). Where and insofar as a decree is for the payment of money, the Court may, in the decree, order interest at such rate as the Court deems reasonable to be paid on the principal sum adjudged, from the date of the suit to the date of the decree, in addition to any interest adjudged on such principal sum for any period prior to the institution of the suit, with further interest at such rate as the Court deems reasonable on the aggregate sum so adjudged, from the date of the decree to the date of payment, or to such earlier date as the Court thinks fit.

(2) Where such a decree is silent with respect to the payment of further interest on such aggregate sum as aforesaid from the date of the decree to the date of payment or other earlier date, the Court shall be deemed to have refused such interest, and a separate suit therefore shall not lie."

10. On a plain reading of section 34(1) we find that law contemplates separate interest for three different stages which may be awarded by a Court where and insofar as decree is for the payment of money. The Court may order interest to be paid on the principal sum adjudged (1) from the date of the suit to the date of the decree, in addition to (2) any interest adjudged on such principal sum for any period to the institution of the suit with (3) further interest on the aggregate sum so adjudged from the date of the decree to the date of payment, or to such earlier date as the Court thinks fit.

11. "Sub-section (2) clearly refers to the interest mentioned in item 3) above i.e. interest from the date of the decree and says that if a decree is silent with respect to such interest the Court shall be deemed to have refused the same, and a separate suit therefore, shall not lie.

<u>12. We find that this power of awarding interest by the Court is a discretionary one but the question is, whether this discretionary power of the Court is an unfettered one has to be construed in the light of the facts and circumstances of a particular case. Certainly this discretion, in our view, is to be exercised judiciously and not capriciously.</u>

<u>13. This view of ours finds support in the decision of Chalna Marine Products Ltd vs Reliance Insurance 50 DLR (AD) 100 wherein the Appellate Division after taking into account section 478 of the Insurance Act, 1938 as amended, which provides for granting of interest on claims, maintained:-</u>

<u>"This provision displaces the discretion of the Court conferred by section 34 of the Code of Civil Procedure in the matter of granting interest. Hence the plaintiff-appellant is entitled to the statutory interest under section 478 of the Insurance Act. The Court has no discretion in the matter."</u>

<u>14. In the instant case also as we have already discussed, the Court is left with no choice but to award interest as per law. Since from the evidence on record it is found that defendant-respondent had enough money to repay the loan with interest. This fact displaces the discretion of the Court conferred by section 34 of the Code of Civil Procedure in the matter of granting interest.</u>

<u>15. In the case as referred to above discretion was displaced by the apex Court considering section 478 of the Insurance Act, 1938. Here in this case this Division displaces the discretion of granting interest under section 34(1), Civil Procedure Code considering the admitted factual position of the case itself. Thakur vs Amolok, AIR 1963 (Raj) 1993 is also on the same point.</u>

16. In view of the discussion as made above we find merit in this appeal.

17. In the result, the appeal is allowed without any order as to cost. The judgment and decree appealed against is modified. The plaintiff does get the decree amounting to Taka 9,18,219.65 with pendente lite interest and any interest adjudged on such principal sum for any period to the institution of the suit at the rate of 15% per annum till realisation.

18. Send down the LC record at once.

Communicate this order at once.

End.

full_judgment:
Siddiqur Rahman Miah J: This revisional application under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure at the instance of defendant- appellant petitioner is directed against the judgment and decree dated 16-2-2004 passed by the learned District Judge, Tangail in Family Appeal No. 37 of 2002 affirming the judgment and decree dated 17-10-2002 passed by the learned Assistant Judge and Family Judge, Sadar Tangail in Family Case No. 11 of 1999 decreeing the case.

2. The plaintiff-opposite party Most Rokshana Choudhury (Sanda) filed Family Suit No. 11 of 1999 in the Court of the learned Senior Assistant Judge, Sadar and Family Judge, Tangail praying for declaration that the divorce dated 22-5-1998, 22-6-1998 and 22-7-1998 is illegal and void and for restitution of conjugal life and also further prayed for a decree of dower of Taka 3,00,000 and for maintenance at the rate of Taka 5,000 per month.

3. Facts leading to this Rule, in brief, are that the opposite party No.1 Most Rokshana Choudhury (Sanda) filed Family Suit No. 11 of 1999 in the Court of Senior Assistant Judge Sadar and Family Court Judge, Tangail impleading the petitioner Kazi Rashed Akhter Shahid (Prince) and others as defendants stating, inter alia, that opposite party No. 1 Kazi Rashed Akhter Shahid (Prince) and plaintiff No.1 Most Rokshana Choudhury (Sanda) got them- selves married through Registered Kabinnama dated 11-1-1996 at dower of Taka. 3,00,000 and marriage was consummated; that both lived as husband and wife and that defendant-petitioner at the instigation of his parents and relations left plaintiff-opposite party Most Rokshana Choudhury (Sanda) in her father's house since 28-3-1998 and did not pay a single farthing for her maintenance. It is further stated in ,the plaint that the defendant-petitioner sent Talaq nama to the effect that she has been divorced on 22-7-1998 and hence this suit.

4. The defendant-petitioner Kazi Rashed Akhter Shahid (prince) appeared in the Family Suit No. 11 of 1999 in Tangail Sadar Assistant Judge and Family Judge Court and submitted written statement stating, inter alia, that the Kabin Nama was created illegally; that dower money shown therein is the product of forgery; that it was Taka 30,000 only, that the marriage was not consummated, that there has been no marriage and the defendant became victim of fraudulent activities of the guardian of the plaintiff. It is further stated that the defendant is a man of Jessore and there was no reason of his marriage at Tangail and that his guardian or relations were not present in the so-called marriage demanded by the plaintiff and, as such, the judgment and decree dated 17-10-2002 was liable to be set aside allowing this revision.

5. It appears from record that the Family Suit No. 11 of 1999 was filed on 1-3-1999 and the suit was fixed for ex parte hearing on 20-4-1999. Later on the learned trial Court decreed the suit ex parte on 2-6-1999.

6. The defendant-petitioner filed Miscellaneous Case No. 57 of 1999 under Order XLVII, rules 1 and 2 on 8-6-1999. The Miscellaneous case was allowed on 7-7-1999 and the case was restored to its original file and number. Again, due to nonappearance of the defendant, the suit was fixed for ex parte hearing on 17-10-2002.

7. The plaintiff herself deposed as PW 1 stating that they got themselves married through registered Kabinnama on 11-1-1996, at a dower of Taka 3,000 and the marriage was consummated as they lived together as husband and wife. She further deposed that the talaq dated 22-7-1998 was not effected as the notice of talaq was not at all served on the Chairman as well as on her and the talaq remained invalid and illegal. She proved the certified copy of Kabinnama and an attested copy of talaqnama which have been marked Exhibit 1 and 1(ka) respectively.

8. The learned Assistant Judge and Family Judge, Sadar Tangail on consideration of the facts and circumstances of the case and evidence on record decreed the suit ex parte on 17-10-2002 allowing the prayer for restoration of conjugal right granting dower of Taka 1,50,000 and maintenance of Taka 55,000.

9. Being aggrieved by the judgment and decree dated 17-10-2002, the defendant preferred appeal being No. 37 of 2002 before the learned District Judge, Tangail who also considering the evidence on record affirmed the judgment and decree of the learned Assistant Judge and Family Judge by his judgment and decree dated 16-2-2004.

10. It is against the aforesaid judgment and decree dated 16-2-2004, the petitioner moved this Court and obtained the present Rule.

11. Mr HM Borhan, the learned Advocate for the petitioner, submits that the learned District Judge, Tangail passed the judgment and decree without going deep into the facts and circumstances of the case and the laws applicable thereto; that the judgment and decree passed by the learned District Judge, Tangail is slipshod and did not reveal the facts and legal consequences involved in the case; that the learned District Judge Tangail did not consider the Talaq given by the defendant petitioner to the plaintiff-opposite party in its true and legal perspective, that the learned District Judge, did not consider the social and economic position of the defendant-petitioner nor enquired about the income of the petitioner and that the learned District Judge ought to have seen that dower amount of the marriage, if any, according to her status cannot be more than 30,000 (thirty thousand). He further submits that the judgment and decree passed by the learned lower Court are neither proper nor in accordance with law and, as such, the impugned judgment and decree caused serious injury to the petitioner occasioning failure of justice.

12. The learned Advocate for the petitioner referred the case of Serajul Islam vs Helana Begum and others reported in 48 DLR 48 in support of his contention.

13. Mr Abul Quashem, the learned Advocate for the opposite party, on the other hand, submits that the plaintiff-respondent-opposite party as plaintiff instituted Family Suit No. 11 of 1999 in the Court of the learned Senior Assistant Judge Sadar and Family Court Judge, Tangail, against the defendant-appellant-petitioner stating that he married the plaintiff by registered kabinnama dated 11-1-1996 at a dower of Taka 3,00,000, that they lived together as husband and wife whereby the said marriage was duly consummated; that at the instigation of the parents; the defendant left the plaintiff-opposite party at the house of her father at Tangail since 28-3-1998 uncared for and did not pay a single farthing towards her maintenance and that the notices of the Talaqnama dated 22-7-1998 were not at all served on the chairman as well as on the opposite party and, as such, the so-called talaq is invalid and illegal.

14. Mr Abul Quashem further submits that on receipt of summons the defendant contested the said family suit by filing written statement denying the case of the plaintiff alleging, inter alia, that the Kabinnama was the product of forgery. Thereafter several dates for pre emptory hearing were fixed but the contesting defendant failed to attend the Court nor did take any step on any of the dates of hearing and thus the trial Court decreed the suit against the defendant considering the facts of the case and evidence on record by his judgment and decree dated 17-2-2002.

15. It is further stated that against the said judgment and decree Of the trial Court, the defendant preferred Family Appeal No. 37 of 2002 before the learned District Judge, Tangail, which was dismissed on contest. Mr Quashem further submitted that the learned District Judge was perfectly justified in affirming the judgment and decree of the trial Court and the concurrent finding of the Courts below does not suffer from any illegality and legal infirmity to justify interference by this Court in revision.

16. We have heard the learned Advocates of the parties at length and perused the revisional application, counter-affidavit and the impugned judgments of the Courts below. The whole argument of the learned Advocate for the petitioner was that Talaq pronounced by the petitioner has become effective and the marriage between the parties has been terminated.

17. Now the point for determination is, whether the talaq pronounced by the petitioner has become effective and whether the marriage between the parties has been dissolved or not.

18. In order to consider this point, it is necessary to refer section 7 of the Muslim Family Laws Ordinance of 1961 and to see whether the provision of this section has been complied with or not.

19. Section 7 of the Muslim Family Laws Ordinance of 1961 reads as follows:

"Talaq: 7(1) Any man who wishes to divorce his wife shall, as soon as may be after the pronouncement of talaq in any form whatsoever, give the Chairman notice in writing of his having done so, and shall supply a copy thereof to the wife.

(2) Whoever contravenes the provisions of sub-section (1) shall be punishable with simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to one year or With fine which may extend to ten thousand taka or with both.

(3) Save as provided in sub-section(5) a talaq, unless revoked earlier, expressly or otherwise, shall not be effective until the expiration of ninety days from the day on which notice under sub-section (1) is delivered to the Chairman.

(4) Within thirty days of the receipt of notice under sub-section (1) the Chairman shall constitute an Arbitration Council for the purpose of bringing about a reconciliation between the parties and the Arbitration council shall take all steps necessary to bring about such reconciliation.

(5) If the wife be pregnant at the time talaq is pronounced, talaq shall not be effective until the period mentioned in sub-section (3) or the pregnancy, whichever be later, ends.

(6) Nothing shall debar a wife whose marriage has been terminated by talaq effective under this section from remarrying the same husband, without an intervening marriage with a third person, unless such termination is for the third time so effective."

20. Before the promulgation of the Muslim Family Laws Ordinance, the talaq could be effective simply by its pronouncement as prescribed under the Muslim law without giving any written notice to the wife and the Chairman. The Muslim Family Laws Ordinance for the purpose of effecting the talaq has provided that the giving of notice in writing to the Chairman, a copy thereof to the wife is mandatory. Similar view has been expressed in 15 DLR(SC) 9 and PLD (1963) (SC)51.

21. No talaq will be effective if the notice is served upon the Chairman by the husband. Notice is to be given to the Chairman where the wife to whom divorce has been pronounced was residing at the time of its pronouncement. The jurisdiction is determined by the residence of the wife and not by the place where the marriage was contracted or where the couple last resided together. It is not even in the permanent residence of the wife.

<u>22. A talaq not coupled with notice to the chairman of the union or paurashava will not operate as a valid talaq. A divorce thus given by the husband is not effective on account of non service of notice under the Ordinance and not having been established by him to have been given to the Chairman. The non-compliance of issuing of this notice makes the Talaq ineffective The sub-section (1) of section 7 requires the husband to give a notice in writing of his having pronounced talaq. But if the husband abstains himself from issuing such notice to the Chairman, it would be deemed that the husband has revoked the talaq and the marital status of the parties has not been changed.</u>

23. Sub-section 3 of section 7 of the Ordinance, introduces the effectiveness of talaq concluded by any of the approved modes with the expiry of 90 days to be reckoned from the date when the chairman received the notice of talaq addressed to him. Ninety days reconciliation period is to start from the date of the receipt of notice by the Chairman and not from the date when it was written. We find support of the above view in the decision reported in PLD 1977 Lah 1193

24. In the instant case the petitioner has totally failed to prove by any convincing  evidence that the notice of talaq was sent to the chairman and a copy thereof to the opposite party. A talaq will not be effective even after the expiry of 90 days if any of the conditions of effectiveness of talaq i.e. pronouncement as per Mohammedan Law, service of notice on chairman and a copy thereof to wife is not complied with. The chairman, on receipt of notice addressed to him by the husband, shall constitute an arbitration council headed by him to reconcile the parties. The arbitration council so constituted will be represented by each of the parties by their respective representatives. A reference may be made to the case of PLD(1975) Lah. 466.

25. In the instant case, the petitioner has totally failed to prove that the chairman received such notice. Since it has not been proved that the petitioner issued the notice of talaq to the Chairman, then the constitution of arbitration council to reconcile the parties does not arise.

Hence, the conditions of effectiveness of talaq have not been established.

26. Mr Abul Quashem, the learned Advocate, cited the decision in the case of Shajiqul Islam and others vs State reported in 46 DLR 700 wherein their Lordships decided that a divorce under the Ordinance is not a unilateral act, rather it involves a public authority in the matter. It precludes a divorce or talaq from being effective for a period of ninety days from the date of the receipt of the notice by the Chairman. Consequently, the marital status of the parties will not in any way change during that period. The parties in law will continue to remain husband and wife till the divorce is confirmed. In the instant case the petitioner has totally failed to prove that the notice upon the chairman was served and that the Chairman constituted an arbitration council to reconcile the matter.

27. Mr Abul Quashem, the learned Advocate for the opposite party, has strongly argued that the petitioner did not at all issue and serve any notice of divorce to the Chairman and a copy thereof to the opposite party. He further argued that mere non service of notice upon the Chairman under the Ordinance of 1961 will render the talaq ineffective and, as such, the marriage will subsist. We find much force in his argument.

<u>28. In the instant case it appears that defendant Kazi Rashed Akhter Shahid (prince) married the plaintiff by registered kabinnama on 11-1-1996; that at the instigation of his parents he left the plaintiff Most Rokshana Choudhury (Sanda) at the house of her father since 28-3-1998 uncared for and did not pay a single farthing towards her maintenance; the petitioner did neither try to bring her nor did he maintain his wife. It is fully an unkind attitude of the petitioner towards his wife. The Muslim Family Law Ordinance, 1961 is a beneficial legislation. The object of the provision of this Ordinance is certainly for the benefit of the vast majority of a particular class of people. From the reading of section 7 of the said Ordinance the object of the said section is to give a benefit to the female preventing a hasty dissolution of marriage by talaq being pronounced by the husband unilaterally without giving any scope for reconsideration but such benevolent intention is likely to be converted into an instrument of abuse and tyranny by the husband instead of preventing the said abuse may aggravate the suffering without end. On plain reading of section 7 of the Ordinance 1961, it can be said that it was never the intention of the legislature that a husband exercising his independent act pronouncing talaq cannot be given effect to until and unless such notice is given to the chairman and it means if a husband divorces his wife but does not give notice purposely to the chairman then the divorce will not be effective till eternity. The intention of the legislature while enacting the said Ordinance 1961 was to prevent hasty dissolution of marriage and a duty is cast upon the husband to give notice under section 7 of the said Ordinance. If he failed to do so intentionally the very object of the said section becomes redundant. In this case, the petitioner at the instigation of his parents, left his wife at the house of her father at Tangail since 28-3-1998 uncared for and did not pay a single farthing towards her maintenance. It further appears that the petitioner contested the suit but he adopted dilatory tactics to harass the opposite party. It shows that he purposely avoided to give notice to the Chairman of Tangail Municipality, so question of reconciling was not held. All these unfair activities of the petitioner made her life miserable.</u>

29. It has been alleged in the Talaqnama that the character of his wife is bad and she is engaged in unsocial activities. But the defendant-petitioner has totally failed to prove such allegation against his wife. There is no such allegation that his wife is unwilling to live with her husband. The wife always wants to go to her husband and; as such, she prays for restitution of conjugal right. Thus, the grounds of talaq have not been proved nor the legal requirement for effecting talaq has been fulfilled.

30. On the other hand, the opposite party Most. Rokshana Choudhury (Sanda) adducing herself as PW 1 and filling a copy of kabinnama and the attested photo copy of the Talaq which are marked Exhibit 1 and 1(ka), in support of her contention, has succeeded in proving that the Talaqnama on 22-7-1998 is illegal and void and she is entitled to restitution of her conjugal right.

31. Now we turn to the question of maintenance prayed for by the opposite party. In order to consider the question of maintenance, reference may be made to section 5 of the Muslim Family Court Ordinance 1985 which deals with jurisdiction of Family Court which runs as follows:

"5. Jurisdiction of Family Courts- Subject to the provisions of the Muslim Family Laws Ordinance 1961 (VII of 1961) a Family Court shall have exclusive jurisdiction to entertain, try and dispose of any suit relating to, or arising out of, all or any of the following matters namely,

(a) dissolution of marriage;

(b) restitution of conjugal rights;

(c) dower;

(d) maintenance;

(e) guardianship and custody of children"

32. In the instant case, the plaintiff Most. Rokshana Choudhury (Sanda) as PW 1 deposed that the, petitioner, at the instigation of his parents, left her in her father's house at Tangail since 28-3-1998 uncared for and did not pay a single farthing towards her maintenance. The petitioner has totally failed. to show any evidence to the effect that he gave any maintenance to his wife.

33. It could not be established that the plaintiff-opposite party ever refused to come to the domain of her husband to perform her marital obligation and to obey him. But it appears that for no fault Of the opposite party, the petitioner was neglecting her and left her in the house of her father since 28-3-1998 and refused to maintain her since that date. Hence, it can be safely decided that the plaintiff-opposite party is entitled to get maintenance from her husband as the marriage between them still subsists.

34. The main argument which formed the basis of the Hanafi view is that Hinda, the wife of Abu Sufian approached the Holy Prophet (SM) complaining about her inadequate maintenance by Abu Sufian, when the Prophet ordered her husband to pay so much as was sufficient to maintain her. Another incident is that Caliph Umar wrote to his army officers in distant counties that the Muslim soldiers who were away from their wives should be ordered either to give maintenance to their wives or divorce them. It was further directed that in the event of divorce, they should also remit arrears of past maintenance. It is not disputed that no exception was taken, to this direction of Caliph Umar.

35. Upon the consideration of the above facts and in the light of direction of Prophet (SM) and caliph, it can be safely held that the maintenance of a wife is the bounden duty of a husband, when the wife is loyal to her.

36. Considering the aforesaid statutory provisions and in view of above decisions cited above, we do not find any reason to hold otherwise. Accordingly, it is held that the Court has the jurisdiction to pass a decree for past maintenance in an appropriate case like the instant one and the Court below has committed no illegality in passing the decree for maintenance for plaintiff-opposite party.

37. The learned Advocate for the petitioner has referred the case of Serajul Islam vs Helana Begum and others reported in 48 DLR 48 in support of his contention. In our case under review since it has been proved that the service of notice upon the Chairman and other requirement of law were not at all proved and thus the marriage subsists. So, the facts and circumstances of the cited case of the petitioner are quite distinguishable from the present case, as such, cited cases are of no assistance of the petitioner.

38. In the facts of the case we have no hesitation to form opinion that the appellate Court rightly applied his judicial mind and passed the impugned judgment and decree dated 16-2-2004.in Family Appeal No. 37 of 2002 affirming the judgment and decree dated 17-10-2002 passed by the learned Senior Assistant. Judge and Family Judge, Sadar Tangail in Family Suit No. 11 of 1999. He passed the impugned judgment and decree assigning genuine reasons. We do not find any illegality and legal infirmity in the impugned judgment and decree occasioning failure of justice to justify interference by this Court exercising revisional jurisdiction under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure.

39. We find no substance in this Rule.

40. In the result, the Rule is discharged without any order as to cost. The judgment and decree dated 16-2-2004 passed by the learned District Judge, Tangail in Family Appeal No. 37 of 2002 affirming the judgment and decree dated 17-10-2002 passed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge and Family Court Judge, Sadar Tangail is affirmed and the suit is decreed.

41. The order of stay granted at the time of issuance of the Rule is hereby recalled and vacated.

Send down the LCR at once.

End.
